title: Motorizare DualAx pentru EQ5
description:
Motorizarea pe ambele axe este foarte utilă când observați diferite zone ale Lunii sau când încercați să găsiți diferite obiecte pentru astrofotografie. După ce centrați un obiect în câmpul vizual, este foarte convenabil să folosiți unitatea de control pentru a mișca ușor telescopul, de exemplu pentru a explora diferite zone ale Lunii. Sistemul dual axis permite de asemenea menținerea unui obiect în centru în timpul astrofotografiei. Unitatea de control are viteze de 2x, 8x, 16x. Folosiți viteza 2x pentru o deplasare ușoară în timpul fotografiei și celelalte viteze mai mari pentru a găsi sau centra obiectele. Montarea kitului este foarte simplă. Tensiunea necesară este de 6V (compartimentul pentru baterii este inclus). Pentru o urmărire corectă este nevoie de o aliniere polară cât mai precisă.

title: ERS-EO IOD-A - LOW LUMINANCE / NIGHT VISION
description: In order to de-risk and accelerate the implementation phase of EOGS, the IOD/IOV activities will focus on short-term achievements delivered through targeted in-orbit experiments. These experiments are intended to provide early proof of concept and in-orbit validation, with demonstrable results available ahead of the next Ministerial Conference in 2028.The scope and objectives of the IOD/IOV activities are aimed at strengthening European autonomy, including enhancing the industrialisation of solutions already under development, and supporting pre-operational validation and technology demonstration.The technologies to be developed for EOGS space missions will be selected in consultation with the European Commission and Participating States, and in accordance with the main findingsof the EOGS studies. The technologies which are being considered are:- Secure inter-satellite links and IRIS interoperability;- Data management, on-board processing and dynamic satellite tasking to reduce latency;- Enhanced security features demonstrating resilience to the considered threats;- Serialisation and synergies (re-use) across the ERS fleet;- Increased agility and imaging capacity over crisis area;- Low-cost high-performance SAR and optical payloads with extended imaging capabilities; and- Platforms optimised for batch launches on European launchers and compatible with applicable clean space policies.Drawing on these findings, together with further consultation with industry through the Request for Information (RFI) released in July 2025 which received a substantial number of responses four main themes have been identified for the IOD/IOV activities.The In-Orbit Demonstration/Validation(IOD/IOV) activities are therefore organised into the following four themes:A. IOD-A: Low Luminance / Night VisionB. IOD-B: DynamicSatellite TaskingC. IOD-C: Reduced information age (i.e. data latency from acquisition to product delivery)D. IOD-D: Satellite Super AgilityThese correspond to areas where a further consolidation is needed (hence the relevance of conducting an IOD) before a feature of very high interest and relevance to the ERS-EO programme objective could be declared operational and included in the nominal configuration of the system.

title: PROCUREMENT OF THE LISA TELESCOPE ASSEMBLY
description: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) is the first space mission designed to observe theuniverse via gravitational waves, ripples in the fabric of space time caused by the acceleration ofmassive objects in the universe. The LISA observatory consists of three identical spacecraft (eachwith a mass/power of about 2700Kg/>3kW), forming an equilateral triangular constellation of 2.5million km side-length, in trailing or leading orbit with respect to the Earth at about 50 million km. Thepassage of a gravitational wave results in a modulation of the length of one arm with respect toanother, which is detected using laser interferometry.ESA is responsible for the mission, including procurement of the spacecraft and the launch vehicletogether with the development of the ground segment to control and operate the spacecraft (fromthe Mission Operation Centre - MOC) and to perform the science mission planning and process thedata products, including archiving (from the Science Operation Centre - SOC). The ESA MemberStates and NASA contribute to the mission with several payload elements (ESA CFI to the Prime).ESA has also the overall responsibility of the verification of the mission performance.For each spacecraft, the LISA Telescope Assembly (LTA) consists of two ultra-stable Zerodurtelescopes. Each telescope is mounted on the Moving Optical Subassembly (MOSA), which hostsall the optical elements.The Executive believes it prudent to take action now to limit any potential damage to the Programmestemming from the unstable situation with NASA. Acknowledging the urgency of the situation, theSPC has requested the Executive to investigate European industrial solutions. This paper outlinesthe approach being taken by the Executive to fulfil this action.Although there have not been specific technology development activities on a LISA Telescope, allthe Large Space Integrators in Europe have amply demonstrated substantial capabilities to designand procure complex telescopes in several flying Scientific Missions. The Executive is thereforeconfident that European Industry can provide the LISA Telescope Assembly as per requirementsand in the needed timeframe.Several industrial discussions have taken place during July and August, that allowed the Executiveto refine the original cost estimates and get confirmation about the throughput rate necessary tomeet the LISA needs.The Executive intends to proceed with the release of an open, competitive tendering for the provisionof the Telescope Assembly for the three LISA spacecraft, with three different contractual phases tobe activated according to the evolution of the geopolitical scenario: Phase 1 ending with initial testing of the breadboard model expected Q4-26. (The activitymay be stopped at this point and transferred under national funding.) Phase 2 ending at the delivery of the Qualification Model (TRL8) expected in 2029, Phase 3 ending at the delivery of the Flight HW for one spacecraft (activation of the Phase 3foreseen at the end of 2028) expected in 2031 Phase 4 ending at the delivery of the hardware for the 3 spacecraft (activation of the Phase4 foreseen at the end of 2028, but possible also later if required).The Executive would like to highlight that the above phasing should not be interpreted as rigidlyconsequential, e.g. Phase 3 can be activated prior to the completion of phase 2. The approach isaimed at positioning the European industry to produce flight hardware at contained risk from 2029(as TRL8 achieved) and safeguard the overall LISA schedule.The Executive expects that the primes will have to involve highly specialised companies (for opticalmachining and polishing), with a traditional strong expertise in France. The material supply forZerodur is single source in Germany. The Executive estimates that, with the majority of the supply chain pre-selected at the time of the proposal in these countries, there is about 15-20% opportunitiesfor economic operators from outside the Big-4 (e.g. OGSE, facilities).The envisaged timescale for the present procurement is as follows: 24 September 2025 IPC Procurement Proposal approval Sep 2025 ITT preparation and release Oct/Nov 2025 Bid preparation Dec 2025 Bid evaluation Dec 2025, endorsement by Special SPC 28 January 2026 Contract Proposal approval at IPC February 2026 Negotiations and contract KOWith this timescale, and the kick-off of the industrial activities in February, the Executive expects todemonstrate TRL6 in 2027 and achieve TRL8 in 2029 (with Qualification Model).Given the status of the LISA Project, the Executive does not foresee any specific geo-returnrequirements for this procurement. However, the ITT will include a preference clause for underreturned countries in the Science Programme.In addition, the Tenderers will be requested to favour the participation of SMEs and Midcaps in theirconsortium and demonstrate pursuing such involvement e.g. by using esa-star communicationfeatures, RFIs or other means.

title: M2 PCIE NVME SOLID STATE DRIVES FOR FUTURE MASS STORAGE SOLUTIONS EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a memory array based on M2 PCIe NAND flash memory Solid State Drives modules and characterise the radiation effects and possible mitigation methods at software and hardware levels.Description: High density Mass storage solutions based on NAND flash memory Solid State Drives (SSD) are widely used in data server applications and present a great opportunity for space applications. However, their reliability and their tolerance to radiation-induced effects have not been evaluated so far. M2 PCI ExpressNon-Volatile Memory (NVM) storage drives are now commonly used System on Module (SoM) devices, similar in size to Double Dada Rate (DDR) memory modules used in personal computers, and capable of storing over 1TB of data. These SoMs incorporate advanced Error Detection and Correction (EDAC) systems to manage the frequent occurrence of bad blocks and bits in 3D NAND Flash Memories. These devicescan be used in a Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) due to Peripheral Component Interconnect Express (PCIe) interface. Thecombination of powerful EDAC and the hot redundancy of RAID is beneficial for addressing the anticipated radiation effects and wearout in NAND Flash memories when used in Space. The non-volatile nature of these memories helps preventing data loss during power cycling to recover Single Event Functional Interrupts (SEFI) in the control electronics. Additionally, these storage drives are currently used in high-speed computation nodes where radiation effects caused by neutrons and alpha particles are a concern. The PCIe interface is widely supported in commercial processors and FPGAs, and will be featured in the next generation of space-graded processorsand FPGAs. The PCIe interface targets to enable the use of very high density, compact, non-volatile memories modules, for the nextgeneration platform and payload units (OBCs, solid state mass memories, ICUs, etc). This proposal aims to develop a RAID array controlled by a European processor or FPGA (Field Programmable Gate Arrays), using various M2 PCIe NVMe SSD modules. This setup enables the assessment of feasibility and reliability concerning radiation and wear out effects, paving the way for a new concept of extremelyhigh-density data storage for space applications. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Selection of several candidateM2 PCIe SSD devices from different manufacturers. - Development of a Single Event Effect (SEE) test setup for SSD drives using thePCIe compatible European processor / FPGA in RAID configuration. - Proton and heavy ion SEE testing- Assessment of the test results and proposal of further mitigation techniques if needed.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: I-HAB - High Capacity Mass Memory (HCMM)
description:
The Cislunar Gateway – International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESA’s contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization requirements from 2025. The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and Canada. 

The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a ‘basecamp’ for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor High Capacity Mass Memory (HCMM for I-HAB in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

The High Capacity Mass Memory will be part of the Avionics subsystem.
The HCMM corresponds to the user memory function of the GATEWAY hosting the data recorded during all the missions by the astronauts.
The High Capacity Mass Memory is expected to be compatible with Human Factors for Human Space Flight.

Further information concerning the I-HAB campaign can be found on the Agency’s website here:
https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon

Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of geographical return requirements/targets to be considered.

title: HYDRON MARITIME: SATELLITE OPTICAL NETWORK EXTENSION (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3A.239) EXPRO+
description: Objective:The objective of this study is to develop a system concept evolving HydRON services to maritime communications and identify the technology gaps as well as the required development roadmap.Targeted Improvements:To enable maritime communications with satellite HydRON (High-throughput Optical Network) systemDescription:Maritime routes are strategic in a connected world, where economies are interdependent. 80% of the global trade depends on shipping. Current strategical routes include South China, South India, Suez Canal, Mediterranean see, trans-Atlantic and Panama Canal. Together with the current routes, the transit along the arctic seais currently becoming more attention for cargo ships but also for defence purposes. Climate change may enable the use of this route,which could mean a drastic reduction in transport costs and service time (reduction of 25-40% in distance). From a logistics perspective, cargo companies aim to monitor their goods and containers, while ports seek to receive advance information about incoming cargo to optimize and plan the unloading process.Additional to the commercial and logistic interests, the defence aspects connected to maritime communications are of special interest, especially in an arctic route, where any developed infrastructure, could enhanceresilience.Currently, maritime communications relay on low-data rate satellite communications, or the use of low-band frequencies, when the ships are located close to shore. HydRON provides space-space and space-ground connectivity, extending terrestrial networksin space and providing global coverage.The activity shall investigate user needs, requirements and system concepts for maritimecommunications (space-sea, sea-sea, sea-shore/ports), to extend the use of HydRON in maritime scenarios. Technology gaps and related technology roadmaps shall be developed, considering optical terminals and any critical technologies. The system shall consider themanagement of cloud-blockage by combining space communications with e.g. a maritime ship-to-ship free-space network or hybrid communications with RF. The space segment shall consider the coverage along the most used routes. The concept shall consider the combination of security sensitive communications with logistic traffic. Finally, the activity shall propose a demonstrator where the relevant technology as well as the operational concept can be demonstrated. The activity will also contribute to the evolution of ESTOL.

title: Germany – Pharmaceutical products – Abschluss einer nicht-exklusiven Rabattvereinbarung nach § 130a Abs. 8 SGB V zum Wirkstoff Sumatriptan (ausgenommen Filmtabletten und Tabletten), ATC N02CC01 für die Zeit 01.12.2025 - 30.11.2027
description: § 130a Absatz 8 SGB V ermöglicht den Krankenkassen und pharmazeutischen Unternehmen, Rahmenrabattverträge über die zu Lasten der gesetzlichen Krankenkassen abzugebenden Arzneimittel zuschließen. In Hinblick auf die dafür einschlägigen gesetzlichen Vorschriften zur Vergabe öffentlicher Aufträge, findet ein regelmäßiger Prozess wirkstoffbezogener, förmlicher Vergabeverfahren nach den Regularien des 4. Teils des GWB durch die DAK-Gesundheit statt. Für vom Bieter näher in der Anlage 2 zum Vertrag zu benennende Arzneimittel zu dem o. g. Wirkstoff Sumatriptan (ausgenommen Filmtabletten und Tabletten), ATC N02CC01, beabsichtigt die DAK-Gesundheit, bis zum Inkrafttreten neuer Arzneimittelrabattverträge mit möglichst allen interessierten pharmazeutischen Unternehmen Arzneimittelrabattverträge abzuschließen. Ein Rabattvertrag i.R.d. Zulassungsmodells zu dem o. g. Wirkstoff tritt erstmals am 01.12.2025 in Kraft und endet am 30.11.2027. Er endet unabhängig davon automatisch mit Inkrafttreten des Exklusivvertrages.

title: Bando per l’affidamento dei servizi per progetti di ricerca e sviluppo a tematiche disciplinari relative a “Infrastrutture per la navigazione satellitare”
description: L’Agenzia Spaziale Italiana ha indetto un bando di gara per la realizzazione del progetto di infrastrutture per la navigazione satellitare con lo scopo di realizzare sistemi e infrastrutture di terra di tipo GNSS, basati su nuove tecnologie e concezione, che, sfruttando la potenzialità delle tecniche di radio-localizzazione satellitare, contribuiscano in modo trasversale allo sviluppo nei diversi settori di applicazione in campi quali: trasporti, servizi mass-market (Location Based Services, anche indoor), sincronizzazione delle infrastrutture critiche, agricoltura sostenibile e circolare (precision farming), sorveglianza del territorio/ambiente e IOT. La scadenza è prevista per: 8 marzo 2023 ore 12.00. La scadenza per le domande di chiarimento è il 22 febbraio 2023 ore 12.00
